name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.160.0 — The wireframe register becomes shadcn Neutral's own register: wire-tokens.css declares shadcn's eighteen colour-role names and oklch() values verbatim (fetched from the shadcn registry) plus --radius and three pipeline-local roles, replacing eleven plugin-local names under which --muted meant the opposite of shadcn's own sense. wire.css's fifty-two var() references re-base onto the new names, every border-radius moves onto shadcn's four-step scale, and five primitives (button, badge, card, tabs, sheet) are re-drawn to match the registry source, including a sheet shadow that was passing an opaque surface role as a shadow colour. mocks-driver.js gains --refresh-register, which classifies a host's tokens.css by the role names it declares and migrates a retired-register host onto the current one in one command, renaming every var() reference across design/ via the new spec/scripts/lib/wire-roles.js role map. ADR-0013 is narrowed by backlink (ADR-0016): its eleven-role description of the register becomes eighteen roles under shadcn's own names. 7.159.0 — /spec:doctor check 20 becomes Expiry readiness and gains a second derivation: coverage-scope.js names each host file that parses acceptance-criterion ids beside a done status yet never mentions SHALL CONTINUE TO. Such a check demands a carrier for every criterion of a done spec, contradicts close-time test expiry, and deadlocks every close once the close deletes those tests — the remedy is to scope its carriers to specs that are not done, per the grounding contract's § Test expiry. The scan runs whether or not the tree holds retirable tests, because the deadlock is a property of the gate rather than of today's retirable count; it is a conformance probe for hosts initialized before the contract carried that section, not a recurrence-earned guard, and it can be deleted once no readable host reports a finding across a full major version. 7.158.0 — Host gates must exempt done specs from per-AC test coverage, and a close-time red gate says so. The grounding contract gains a required § Test expiry: a check requiring a test carrier per acceptance criterion scopes its carriers to specs that are not done, because close deletes a spec's own tests and then re-runs the gate over that tree — a host check demanding a carrier for every AC of a done spec deadlocks every close, and relabelling criteria SHALL CONTINUE TO is never the remedy. /spec:init's architecture profiling now checks for such a coverage check while it reads what CI enforces, and the review driver's close-time gate and suite refusals name how many tests expiry just deleted, pointing at the contract section rather than leaving a session to restore the tests it correctly retired.
